summary: Sparks-Allot's Lunar Parking Lot (our Lunar Landing Site Navigator) is an interactive 3D Moon globe that helps mission planners find and compare landing sites. Built on real Barker 5 m/pixel LOLA elevation data with a live 2.6M-row terrain lookup, it lets crews pick any of 11 landing sites — Artemis regions, Cabeus, and Apollo 11 — or click anywhere on the Moon, then plan a traverse across real terrain with live elevation profiles and a gentlest-path option that cuts total ascent by nearly half. Sun and Earth positions come from JPL Horizons ephemeris for any date and time, with Moon Trek illumination and Earth-visibility layers, a Simulate mode that walks the route at up to 32x, and a Surface View showing the ground-level sky, including when the Sun sits behind a ridge. It addresses the challenge by putting terrain, sunlight, and comms in one tool instead of three, so crews can judge a site's safety before committing. For Artemis and beyond, better site selection means safer landings and smarter traverses.
details:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive 3D Moon globe that lets mission planners compare any landing site by date and time. It serves real terrain from Barker 5 m/pixel LOLA DEMs through a live elevation API (2.6M-row lookup) with quantized-mesh 3D terrain, computes Sun and Earth positions from JPL Horizons ephemeris for any date and time, and overlays Moon Trek illumination and Earth-visibility data. A traverse planner draws routes with live elevation profiles and a gentlest-path (A*) option — Shackleton to Cabeus drops from 11,917 m to 6,455 m of total ascent. Simulate mode walks a route at 1x–32x with sunset/Earthset countdowns and terrain-aware Radio/Power indicators (SOLAR/SHADOW/DARK), and Surface View shows the ground-level sky from any point, including when the Sun sits behind a ridge.

The benefit is practical: crews can compare sites for safety, sunlight, and comms before committing, using the same data NASA missions use. The intended impact is safer, better-planned traverses for Artemis crews.

Built with CesiumJS, PHP, MariaDB, and Python tooling. The creative angle: we treat landing-site selection like finding a parking spot — the project is named Sparks-Allot's Lunar Parking Lot — while keeping the science rigorous: real DEMs, real ephemeris, verified against the source data. Factors we weighed: terrain hazards, sunlight and terrain shadow, Earth visibility for comms, traverse difficulty, and making it usable by anyone, not just specialists.
projectRefs: USGS Astrogeology Science Center — Moon base maps (LROC WAC, LOLA shaded relief and color)
